ac:layout-cell.p: Solution summary · API reuse assessment · API calls and Spain changes
Confluence views: Summary · Required behaviour · Sequences and reuse · API reference

This view keeps SPEC016’s RRI, PRI, RSD and RCV meanings and acceptance IDs. The predecessor retains detailed inventories and is unchanged. The 11 November 2026 user decision requires view and user download for public and private platforms, replacing the earlier private-download TBD. File roles and records boundaries remain unchanged. The 13 November 2026 user decision limits DTS conversion to Phase 3 inputs that are not UBL 2.5. Provider coverage and implementation remain open. REF-SCOPE; REF-DTS-SCOPE.

Support two linked journeys. An authorised customer or accountant views the business’s sent and received e-invoices through the ERP. Separately, automatic receiving gets and processes incoming source files, then delivers each eligible invoice once to the authorised ERP. REF-PRODUCT; REF-SCOPE.

In this spec, the Domain Service means the E-Invoice Service reached through the existing E-Invoice API. This name describes access to the capability; it does not define a new API or deployment. Authenticating the caller does not establish permission for the selected business or action. SPFE-S02 Article 11.

tr.td: SPFE public solution — Phase 1
Required: automatic collection, invoice list/detail view and authorised saved-file download.
Missing API/build evidence is a delivery gap; it does not make these outcomes optional.
External private providers — Phase 2
Confirm each provider’s file intake, invoice view and saved-file download before enabling it. The provider transfer mode remains open.
Sage private-platform offering — Phase 3
Confirm the offering, operator role and contracts, including saved-file download, before enabling it.

ac:layout-cell.p: REF-SCOPE records the product decision; REF-PHASE defines the phase labels. RSD-07 requires authorised download of saved invoice files from every enabled platform. Missing provider/API support is a delivery gap; user download remains required. RET-G10 requires evidence of private saved-file download support. A provider may supply files or require Sage to fetch them. That transfer is separate from user download. The selected copy-only policy is in §3.4. REF-COPY-POLICY.

Reuse the dataset and platform setup established by onboarding. Lifecycle owns buyer decisions and payment reports. SPEC014 owns routing and route history. Use GLO-SEI-001 — sending, receiving and invoice roles for direction, sender/recipient, sales/purchase perspective and document type. Viewing does not create buyer acceptance or confirm receipt to a source. A generated readable file and an original structured file keep separate roles.

The customer or authorised accountant uses View invoice list → Select and open invoice for sent and received invoices. The next choices are Download file, Review and take action in SPEC029, or leaving the decision pending. Download is optional. Opening an invoice does not save a file to the user’s device or accept the invoice. The ERP requests the list and invoice details from the Domain Service and displays the results. Automatic incoming collection continues when no customer is signed in. RSD-07; REF-SCOPE.

Reuse the selected business’s existing onboarding setup: business/NIF, test/live environment, platform connections, credential references, authority and dataset mapping. Check receiving, viewing and download permission separately. If the mapping or lookup is missing or unclear, keep the affected work pending. Show its reason, next action and owner. A saved connection or certificate alone does not grant permission.

RET-G01 records the open relationships, with onboarding GAP-01/02/06. No NIF/certificate lookup key or one-dataset-per-NIF rule is selected. Query/Retrieve GETs use datasetId and Sage ID machine-to-machine (M2M) bearer authentication. NIF and certificate are not new GET parameters. SPEC042 defines exact authentication and attachment options.

tr.td: Public collection is due, or the customer requests refresh

Collect eligible invoices automatically, including when no customer is viewing the list. A customer refresh can bring collection forward; combine equivalent refresh requests. A failed query is not an empty successful result. The list-open refresh remains a proposal under §5.
RSD-01–06; A01–03/07/10; REF-PRODUCT, PRD211 Product principles 1–2
Customer/accountant chooses View invoice list

The ERP sends Query e-invoices for the selected business and sent/received scope. The Domain Service checks access and returns permitted invoices, current status, attachment availability and page information. The ERP displays the results and keeps the business/source context across pages. Distinguish an empty list, a failed query and incomplete collection. Show how current SPFE incoming collection is.
RSD-01/03/07; RET-API-01; PRD211 FR30–33/48/52; REF-SCOPE
Customer/accountant chooses Select and open invoice from the list

The ERP sends Retrieve e-invoice with the selected ID and business context. The Domain Service rechecks access and returns details, current status, history and requested attachment information. The ERP displays permitted content and original/faithful-copy/derived-file labels. Explain missing content and the next action. Metadata alone is not a complete invoice view. Viewing saved content does not require a live source response or confirmed ERP delivery.
RSD-07; RET-API-02; RET-G01/08; REF-SCOPE
Customer/accountant chooses Download file from the opened invoice

If file choices or links were omitted, the ERP requests them through Retrieve. Renew a link only when expiry is confirmed. Use the chosen attachment’s returned downloadUrl to get its bytes from the file source. Recheck current file permission, role, safety and integrity, including changes since opening. Explain a refusal or file failure and give a safe next action. Conversion or ERP-delivery failure alone does not block a safe permitted download.
RRI-A05/08; RSD-A04/08/09/14; RCV-A23; RET-API-03; REF-SCOPE
Customer/accountant chooses Review and take action on an opened invoice

Continue in SPEC029’s customer decision journey using the same business and invoice identity. Query/Retrieve remain read operations. SPEC029 defines allowed actions, decision/report outcomes and recovery. File access does not enable a command. Copy-only action eligibility remains open.
Enabled private provider sends a notification or file reference
Save the source observation, then get the required files. A source observation records what arrived from that source. Missing files remain FETCH_PENDING with an owner.
RRI-A02/03; PRI-01–04; transfer contract to confirm
Enabled private provider supplies complete files
Verify and save the supplied bytes. Do not fetch them again because later processing is slow.
RRI-A01; RSD-04/05; transfer contract to confirm
Duplicate item or public faithful copy/private original arrives
Preserve both source observations. Prove that the files represent one business invoice before linking them or delivering one invoice to the ERP. Hold changed content as a conflict.
RSD-A05/06; RCV-A13
Correction document or replacement content arrives
Preserve the original. A correction document has its own identity/reference; replacement content needs a relationship decision. Never overwrite because the invoice number matches.
Capture succeeds; validation, mapping or delivery fails
Recover the affected processing from the saved file. Keep independently permitted saved-file access. Do not claim ERP receipt.
Events are missed or available history is incomplete
Recover a bounded range using existing identities. Keep any unproved coverage gap visible.
RRI-A04; RSD-A10
Client permission or route changes
Stop affected future actions; retain historical context and independent authorised client work. Recheck before resuming.

ac:layout-cell.p: Detailed overall process — Draw.io · PNG.

The diagram expands the SPEC025 combined workflow into proposed responsibilities and handoffs. Its Download file and Review and take action columns are separate choices on the summary's customer-access path. They are not successive steps. E marks the shared problem or pending result in §3.3. S connects safe saved files to viewing before ERP delivery completes. R returns a file through capture, recipient, safety and role checks under §3.4. Implementation coverage remains unconfirmed.
§3.1 defines source acquisition and saved-file access. §3.2 defines receiving checks and ERP delivery. §3.4 owns the source scenarios, copy-only policy and open private-failure recovery decision.

tr.td: RSD-01
Check current permission for the business/action, environment and source connection before protected calls.
RSD-02
Combine equivalent refresh requests and apply approved capacity limits. Only the current collection run may save progress.
RSD-03
Discover invoices within the confirmed scope. Fetch exact source files separately. Save the evidence needed to continue collection. Distinguish an empty successful result from a failure.
Check the provider, caller and delivery mode. Download missing required files. Reuse complete supplied files. Distinguish partial, expired and unsupported results.
RSD-04

Save exact bytes or an approved reference to unchangeable content. Keep the matching hash (integrity value), source, role, profile and time. Check that the file is not empty and can be read. Failed or incomplete capture stays pending with its reason and owner.
RSD-05
Save the receiving classification: the recorded outcome or pending next step for the captured item. A pending handoff needs an owner and prevents the collection page from being marked complete.
RSD-06; PRI-04
Save completed collection progress only after every item has a saved source file and receiving classification, or an approved reason to ignore it. A later mapping failure does not undo this progress.
RSD-08
Recover an authorised, bounded range using existing item identities. Track recovery progress separately. Keep gaps visible when recovery is not possible.
RSD-07

For saved-file view/download from any enabled platform, check current permission, role, safety, integrity and retention. Return labelled saved content and audit the result. Do not relabel a faithful copy or generated readable file as an original.
RSD-09
Apply retention rules and holds that prevent deletion. Preserve permitted historical access. Verify the required exit export before permitted disposal.
RCV-01 Record
Save the source file reference and hash before later work or an irreversible confirmation to the source. If only metadata is available, keep file retrieval pending.
RCV-02 Recipient control at intake

Check the invoice recipient against the existing onboarding setup: business, test/live environment, route at the time of receipt and target ERP. Hold unclear or wrong matches for review; do not show the invoice to another client.
RCV-03 Safety and integrity at intake
Check trust, safety and file integrity. Disable XML external-entity and network access. A check that has not finished has not passed. Keep unsafe files restricted.
RCV-04 Identify the invoice and label the file

Read the source item and invoice references. Label the file as original, faithful copy or another role supported by evidence. For Spain public UBL, use the copy-indicator table. Keep missing or conflicting role evidence unresolved. The indicator does not prove that two files represent the same business invoice. Linking them requires evidence under RET-G04/07/09.
RCV-05 Check format and rules
Check the original against the rules for its received format. Keep invalid, unsupported and unfinished checks separate.
RCV-06 Convert only when needed

Use existing DTS only in Phase 3, when the received invoice is not UBL 2.5. Convert it to UBL 2.5 using a tested mapping. Keep the received original and its link to the converted file. Check the output, including tax and extension fields, before ERP delivery. UBL 2.5 skips conversion in every phase. Other formats in Phases 1–2 stay pending for format resolution. RET-G07 requires evidence of the actual build and mapping. REF-DTS-SCOPE.
RCV-07 Send to the ERP
Save the delivery decision and a stable delivery ID. Verify the ERP confirmation before recording receipt. If the reply is lost, check the original result or resend only when safe, using the same ID.
RCV-08 Confirm to the source
Send a confirmation when the source contract requires it. If the result is unclear, check the original result before repeating a confirmation that may change the source state.
RCV-09 Recover
Record the reason, responsible person or team, and safe next step. Retry only the failed step from the saved file, with the versions recorded. Keep facts already delivered.

ac:layout-cell.p: Implementation support for reusing previous results, resuming duplicate intake and comparing file content remains unconfirmed under SPEC027 RET-G09. The required outcomes above still apply. The R path retrieves a missing original and repeats intake checks. It does not establish automatic matching of original and copy.

Internal approval can hold only the action it governs. Accounting transfer has its own destination and receipt. An accountant’s results stay separate for each client. These activities do not create buyer acceptance or block independently authorised capture. RCV-I13–16; RCV-A26–31.
Recover only the affected work. Keep completed results. Record the reason, original operation, next action, owner and evidence needed to resume. Provider support for these controls still needs proof.

tr.td: Forged, wrong-client, duplicate or late event
Reject untrusted events and wrong-client access. Keep saved observations for repeats. Recover missing work using verified event/item identity.
Events/Security; RRI-A02/04/09
Attempt ERROR; current status unchanged
Read the matching history outcome and error. Follow the action for that code. A notification failure does not require another source capture.
API/Operations; INT-ERR01; RET-G02/09
Expired credentials or withdrawn client permission
Stop affected calls and reads. Resume only with current permission for the business/action. Keep other clients independent.
Identity/client; RSD-A01/08; RCV-A29
Timeout, outage or 429
Keep the original operation and pending result. Honour valid Retry-After. Retry within confirmed safe limits. If the operation may already have changed external state, check its result first.
Integration/Operations; RSD-A10/16
Missing file or expired link
Keep capture pending. Renew a link only when expiry is confirmed. Classify other refusals separately. Verify that the returned file belongs to the intended source item.
Integration/provider; RRI-A02/03/06
Interrupted transfer or incomplete file set
Keep verified files. Recover only missing or failed required files. Do not create another invoice.
Integration/Records; RSD-A03/14
Failed page, expired page token, missed events or incomplete history
Keep the last proved collection progress. Recover the bounded gap separately. A partial page is not complete.
Retrieval/API; RSD-A03/07/10
Concurrent capture, differing copies or changed content
Preserve source observations. Check recipient, profile and business meaning before linking files or delivering one ERP invoice. Hold material conflicts for review.
Receiving/Records; RSD-A05/06
Wrong recipient, unsafe/untrusted/invalid/unsupported file
Deny or restrict the affected access/delivery. Require authorised resolution and passing checks. An ordinary retry cannot release a restricted file.
Routing/Security/Validation; RCV-A17/21/22
Hash/metadata mismatch, storage failure or an outdated run
Keep capture/progress incomplete. Recover the original save and reject outdated progress updates. Require consistent bytes, evidence and classification.
Records/Retrieval; RCV-A15
Validation/mapping unavailable, late or losing information
Resume the saved attempt, or authorise reprocessing with recorded versions. Match the output to its source and rule versions. Preserve completed delivery and safe saved-file access.
Validation/Receiving; DTS only for RCV-06 conversion; RCV-A16–18/22/23
Optional readable-file generation fails
Keep its result separate. A PDF or derived UBL file cannot replace a missing original.
Format/Records; RRI-A06
Required invoice-view content is unavailable
Show the incomplete view, reason and owner. Use a confirmed available source or representation where permitted. Do not invent missing content. Keep safe saved-file access independent.
Product/Format; DTS only if RCV-06 applies; RET-G07/08; REF-SCOPE
ERP rejects delivery, is unavailable or its receipt is lost
Check the original delivery result or safely repeat the same delivery. Confirm ERP receipt. Do not fetch the source again or create another invoice.
Product/Receiving; RCV-A14/15/17
Confirmation to the source may have taken effect
Check the original result before repeating an action that could change source state. If safe checking/repetition is unavailable, keep a manual case with an owner.
Integration/Operations; RSD-A16; RCV-A20
Provider changes or a late item arrives
Keep the original source and route. Confirm the target ERP and current authority. Keep uncertainty visible when a new route is used.
Routing/Product; RCV-A19/28/29
View denied, or saved download interrupted, missing or corrupt
Audit the access result. Retry only with current permission. Missing or corrupt saved files need an integrity/restore case. A missing readable file does not remove access to a safe source file.
Records/Access; RRI-A05/06/08
A hold or provider exit prevents disposal
Keep evidence under hold. Verify the required export before disposal. Preserve permitted historical access.
Records/Compliance; RSD-A11; RCV-A24

ac:layout-cell.p: When the confirmed retry limit is reached, stop automatic retries and keep an unresolved case with an owner. Retry limits and alerts remain open under RSD-G07/RCV-Q11 and RET-G03/09. Escalating to support does not complete the work or permit changes to original files or saved progress. INT-ERR01’s code-specific six-day guidance is not a Spain deadline.

The process shows which file is available, which action can proceed and which work remains pending. The user selected the copy-only access and ERP policy below. Recovery triggers, file-matching rules and copy-only buyer actions remain open. REF-REVIEW; REF-COPY-POLICY.

tr.td: Source capture and collection progress
§3.1 defines completion of collection. Later ERP-processing failure does not undo completed capture. RSD-01–06; PRI-01–04.
Original, faithful-copy and derived-file labels
§4 defines Spain file roles. Apply the selected policy below to ERP delivery. RSD-04; RCV-SPFE-R02.
Invoice identity, validation and repeat handling
RCV-04/05/09 remain distinct. §3.2 records unconfirmed implementation coverage for comparison and reuse of earlier results.
Saved-file access before ERP receipt
RSD-07 and RCV-02/03 govern access after recipient, safety and integrity checks. ERP receipt is not a condition for permitted viewing/download.
Confirmation and recovery
RCV-08 follows the source contract’s timing. §3.3 defines recovery without undoing successful work.

ac:layout-cell.p: If a confirmed original is already saved, continue the required receiving checks without fetching it again. Otherwise, use the source cases below to find a permitted public source or the recipient’s confirmed private connection. Save the returned file. Repeat source, recipient, access, safety and role checks. Prove its relationship to any saved copy before ERP delivery. A returned copy or conflicting role does not complete original retrieval. Hold it for review instead of repeating the same fetch without resolution.

If no permitted source is available, access is denied or retrieval fails, keep original recovery open. Show its reason, next action and owner. ERP delivery stays pending; independently permitted copy access can continue. Automatic recovery triggers, supported source combinations and file-matching rules remain subject to the decisions below. RSD-01/03/04/07; RCV-04/09; REF-COPY-POLICY.

Check the recipient's account activation, current authority and receiving connection before asking the sender. The customer completes missing setup or restores access when prompted. The receiving provider checks invoice availability and delivery where appropriate. If delivery remains unresolved, the customer asks the sender to confirm the destination or make the existing original available through the agreed channel. A sender's confirmation does not change the copy's role or complete file retrieval. After access is restored, retry the confirmed source; a returned file still passes intake and matching checks. A retrieval failure alone does not establish a need to cancel or correct the invoice. RCV-02/09; SPEC025 recovery explanation.

The SPEC025 copy-retrieval explanation describes why labelled copy access continues during this work. It does not enable automatic public-copy fallback or settle copy-only buyer actions; the decisions below retain those limits.

tr.td: A public original is available; no private platform is enabled.
Use confirmed SPFE access to capture the original. Allow permitted saved-file view/download after checks.
Reuse onboarding’s business mapping and access. Resolve missing setup through onboarding. RSD-01/04/07; SPFE-S02 Articles 9–11.
A private platform is enabled and this invoice used public issuance/interconnection.
Capture the original through the confirmed recipient-side path or authorised SPFE recovery.
A private subscription alone does not require a private fetch or change the public original’s role. No separate faithful copy is required for this exchange. Spain scenarios.
Private exchange supplies an original; SPFE supplies a faithful copy.
Capture the private original from the recipient’s confirmed connection or supplied files. Capture the public copy where enabled and available.

Preserve both files. Prove that they represent the same business invoice before linking them. A missing/rejected public copy does not itself invalidate the private original. RCV-04/05; SPFE-S02 Articles 4, 5(6).
Only a public faithful copy is available, with no confirmed private access.
Apply the selected copy-only policy below. Show that the original is unavailable.
Keep original recovery visible with an owner. Knowing the supplier’s provider does not grant access to it. Product/Integration resolves how to get the original.
Private-original retrieval fails; a public faithful copy is independently accessible.
Subject to the recovery-trigger decision below, capture the copy under its own public authority and retain the failed private attempt. Apply the selected copy-only policy.
A refusal for private access is not permission to use another source. No automatic rerouting, original-role substitution or claim that original recovery completed. RSD-01/04; RCV-09.
The private original arrives after the copy, or both arrive concurrently.
Preserve both source observations. Check recipient, identity, profile and business meaning before linking them.
Continue eligible work using the same business invoice identity. Do not create a second ERP invoice. Hold conflicts for review. RSD-A05/06; RCV-A13.

ac:layout-cell.p: Apply this table when Sage holds a faithful copy but has not obtained the original. This does not prove that the sender failed to issue or deliver the original. The copy is part of normal private exchange, not a temporary draft created because retrieval failed. SPFE-S02 Article 4; REF-COPY-REVIEW.

tr.td: View and download
Allow safe authorised access. Label the file Faithful copy and show Original retrieval pending separately. RSD-07; REF-COPY-POLICY.
Automatic ERP intake

Keep delivery into incoming-invoice processing pending until the original passes the required checks. This is the selected product policy, not a general legal restriction on every business action. RCV-04/09; REF-COPY-POLICY.
Approval, commercial rejection, posting and payment

Copy access does not enable these commands. Product/Compliance and Lifecycle must decide each action's eligibility and evidence before enabling it for a copy-only invoice. See the open action decision.
Original recovery
Show the reason, attempted source, next action and owner. Follow original-file retrieval; sender contact is one recovery step, not the only available action. RCV-02/09.
Original arrives later

Repeat intake and matching checks. Preserve the copy, earlier decisions and payment history. Continue under the same verified invoice identity without a second ERP invoice or duplicate report. RCV-04/05/09; RSD-A05/06.
Material disagreement
Preserve both files and their evidence. Hold affected processing for investigation; neither file automatically resolves a conflict. RCV-04/05.
Business status

The files represent one invoice after matching is proved. A copy has no independent second business lifecycle. Keep file role, retrieval progress, business facts and communication results separate. Use qualified current status evidence; a downloaded file does not prove the latest status. SPEC029 status rules.
Required status reports

Assess each report using its own data, authority and qualified process. Do not suspend reporting or reset known facts solely because original retrieval or ERP intake is pending. ES-RD10 Article 12; SPFE-S02 Articles 7–8.
Copy-only access and ERP eligibility — selected
Apply the engineering behaviour table. REF-COPY-POLICY.

Product: reconcile this decision into the canonical PRD before its next baseline review. Records, Receiving and target-product owners: prove file access and later-original handling under RET-G04/07/09/10. This is a product decision, not an external obligation or implementation claim.
copy-only-actionsWhich buyer actions are allowed when only a copy is available? — open

Viewing/downloading a copy does not enable a buyer command. Decide eligibility for each action and the evidence it needs before enabling it. Once original/copy matching is proved, use one business invoice decision and separate reporting results for each destination. Do not treat the files as separate invoices or assume automatic synchronisation. The ERP-delivery hold does not extend a reporting deadline.

Product/Compliance and Lifecycle decide action policy under SPEC029 LCS-R04/12–14 and LIF-G07/08. Receiving/Records prove invoice/file matching under RET-G04/07/09. Evidence must cover copy-first and later-original arrival, action authority, required reporting fields and prevention of duplicate decisions/reports.
When does Sage attempt public-copy recovery after private failure?

Recommend an independently authorised recovery attempt for temporary unavailability or missing bytes. Permission, identity and safety failures retain their own resolution. Keep the private-original case open.
Product/Integration/Identity: select triggers and supported source combinations under RET-G01/03/04/06. No timeout or retry count is selected.
What proves that two files represent one business invoice?
Recommend verified identity and business-meaning checks. Different representations can have different hashes. Material disagreement needs review.

Receiving/Records and product owners: prove comparison rules, required fields and concurrent/late arrival under RET-G04/07/09 and RCV-Q04. If RCV-06 applies, the DTS owner must also prove the selected conversion. Comparing two UBL 2.5 files does not itself require format conversion.

ac:layout-cell.p: Acceptance coverage: extend RSD-A05/06, RRI-A05/08 and RCV-A13/23 for copy-first, original-first, concurrent arrival, private timeout and denied public access. For the original-file decision, check that a saved original avoids another fetch. Files from a permitted public or recipient-private source must pass intake and role checks. Unavailable, denied and failed retrieval must keep recovery open with an owner. Check that missing setup and expired access lead to the correct customer or support action before unresolved delivery is escalated to the sender. A returned copy, sender confirmation or conflicting role must not complete recovery or release ERP delivery. Check the engineering behaviour table, including no implied buyer commands, preserved payment/decision history and independently assessed reporting. Prove one business invoice, separate file roles, no fetch loop and isolation of Spain rules. Recovery-trigger and copy-only action checks depend on the open decisions above. These are required checks, not executed tests. SPFE-S02 Articles 4, 5(6), 7–8, 10–11; REF-COPY-POLICY; REF-COPY-REVIEW.

tr.td: Separate outcomes — RRI-R02; RCV-I10

Discovery, capture, classification, ERP receipt, source acknowledgement and buyer decisions have separate results. Technical errors cannot create Annex II business reports. SPEC029 defines business reporting. Retrieval does not submit the invoice or its faithful copy to SPFE; that belongs to sending.
Public discovery — RSD-SPFE-R01

GetRegisteredInvoice / QUERYBYFILTER: presentation date, up to 1000 results. GetInvoices / QUERYBYID: identity/final state, up to 1000 identifiers. Preserve SECUENCE_ID; continuation is still unqualified. SPFE-S03/S14/S15.
Public file recovery — RSD-SPFE-R02/03

Confirm DownloadInvoicesByLOC or DownloadInvoicesByID separately. The 100-invoice limit applies to ID download only. A locator, invoice identity and MessageId are different identifiers. SPFE-S03/S12/S13.
Recipient authority — RSD-R01
Check representation independently of credentials. Issuer/collaboration or locator-certificate branches do not prove recipient permission. SPFE-S02 Articles 9–11.
Source format — RCV-SPFE-R02
Qualify public UBL 2.5, CopyIndicator, original/copy/derived roles and the conflicting example ProfileID. SPFE-S08/S09.
Shared reuse — RRI-R03/05; RSD-R09; RCV-R14
Test records access and the selected build. DTS conversion follows RCV-06. Keep Spain rules separate from France and other countries.

p.strong: Spain original and faithful copy scenarios — RSD-04; RCV-SPFE-R02

ac:layout-cell.p: For an authorised recipient, use exchange evidence to classify each retrieved file. A file from SPFE can be an original or a faithful copy. Its public source alone does not determine its role.

p.strong: For Spain’s public UBL format, cbc:CopyIndicator means:

tr.td: Copy
false or omitted
Original

ac:layout-cell.p: The exact field is /in:Invoice/cbc:CopyIndicator. Source: final BOE Annex I, BT-ES-1, PDF p. 13, and Article 4(3). SPFE-S02.

Apply this table only to the confirmed Spain public profile. It does not define another country’s or a private platform’s file contract. In that profile, omission means original; outside it, missing role evidence remains unresolved. Conflicting evidence always needs resolution. The indicator labels the file. It does not prove that two files belong to the same invoice. An original and faithful copy need not have identical bytes or differ only in this field. Article 4(2) defines the corresponding invoice information required in the copy. Automatic content comparison remains unconfirmed under §3.2 and RET-G04/07/09. SPFE-S02; SPFE-S08/S09.

tr.td: Sender uses SPFE; recipient uses B2B Router

If the confirmed connection delivers this invoice to B2B Router, obtain the original from B2B Router. No separate faithful copy is required. An authorised recovery from SPFE retains its original role.
SPFE handled issuance or interconnection: SPFE-S02 Article 3(4). B2B Router route, file roles and access remain unconfirmed under RET-G01/04/05.
Sender uses Zerocoma; recipient uses SOVOS; exchange stays private

Obtain the original from SOVOS and the faithful copy from SPFE when available. Preserve both sources. Link them to one business invoice only after their relationship is proved. A missing copy stays visible; it does not relabel or replace the original.

SPFE-S02 Articles 4(1)–(3), 5(5), 6. Names illustrate sender/recipient roles; interoperability, original-file access and copy-result visibility remain unconfirmed under RET-G01/04/05 and sending SND-G05.
Sending has selected the public route and submitted the invoice to SPFE for exchange
Obtain the original from SPFE. Do not expect or create a separate faithful copy for this exchange.
SPFE-S02 Articles 3(4), 5(2). Selection and any existing-copy cancellation remain sending responsibilities under SPEC023 OUT-09/10 and SPFE-S02 Article 5(5).

ac:layout-cell.p: These examples clarify file roles; provider support still needs proof. SPEC023 — OUT-09 Spain recipient-route decision governs a missing private destination, a failed lookup and an explicit public choice. Retrieval does not select a new delivery route. If receiving cannot match the invoice to the exact client, RCV-02 holds it for authorised resolution. It must not send that invoice to SPFE as a fallback.

SPEC027’s evidence gates, including RET-G01 setup mapping, link API evidence to RRI-Q01–03, RSD-G01–09 and RCV-Q01–13. An affected capability cannot be enabled without that evidence. Component boundaries, collection frequency, service targets, retention periods and source-confirmation deadlines remain open.
SPEC027 §3.1 records the proposed list-open refresh and Architecture's pull-policy decisions. It does not make a live SPFE call a condition for viewing captured information.

The reviewed local WSDL baseline is the 23 November 2026 PRE release selected in the source manifest. The release review records unchanged WSDL bytes and added UBL schemas. Newer catalogue and formats replacements still need comparison under the SPEC029 §5.3 source freshness gate. Registration does not prove business-field completeness, provider support or runtime readiness. REF-EVIDENCE.
Required checks below retain their detailed IDs in REF-BASE Part 4. They have not been run against an implementation.

tr.td: RSD-A01/08; RRI-A08; RCV-A27/29
